gloss: to execute; to carry out; to put into practice

definitions.gloss: to execute; to carry out; to put into practice
definitions.explanation: To actually do something that was planned or decided. Emphasizes taking concrete action rather than just thinking or talking about it.

examples.japanese: {計画|けいかく}を{実行|じっこう}する。
{約束|やくそく}したことは{必|かなら}ず{実行|じっこう}しなさい。
examples.english: Always follow through on what you have promised.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}で{決|き}まったことを{来週|らいしゅう}から{実行|じっこう}に{移|うつ}す{予定|よてい}だ。
examples.english: We plan to put into action what was decided at the meeting starting next week.

notes:
A fundamental verb for expressing the act of carrying something out in practice. Contrasts with merely planning, discussing, or intending to do something.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {計画|けいかく}を{実行|じっこう}する: to carry out a plan
- {実行|じっこう}に{移|うつ}す: to put into action
- {実行|じっこう}{力|りょく}: ability to take action; execution ability
- {実行|じっこう}{委員|いいん}{会|かい}: executive committee
- {犯行|はんこう}を{実行|じっこう}する: to carry out a crime

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {遂行|すいこう}する: to carry out — more formal; used for duties and missions
- {実施|じっし}する: to implement — focuses on officially putting a policy or system into effect
- {実践|じっせん}する: to put into practice — emphasizes applying knowledge or theory to real situations
- {執行|しっこう}する: to execute — legal/administrative; carrying out orders, sentences, or duties

REGISTER:
Neutral. Used in both everyday conversation and formal contexts. The noun {実行|じっこう} frequently appears in compound words.
